# Psalm 29 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-psalm of-David. Ascribe to-YHWH, O-sons of-God [bene elim], ascribe to-YHWH glory and-strength.

**2** Ascribe to-YHWH the-glory of-His-name; bow-down to-YHWH in-the-splendor of-holiness.

**3** The-voice of-YHWH [is] over the-waters; the-God of-glory thunders — YHWH over many waters.

**4** The-voice of-YHWH [is] in-power; the-voice of-YHWH [is] in-majesty.

**5** The-voice of-YHWH breaks cedars; YHWH breaks the-cedars of-Lebanon.

**6** And-He-makes-them-skip like-a-calf — Lebanon and-Sirion like-a-young wild-ox.

**7** The-voice of-YHWH hews-out flames of-fire.

**8** The-voice of-YHWH shakes the-wilderness; YHWH shakes the-wilderness of-Kadesh.

**9** The-voice of-YHWH causes-the-deer-to-calve and-strips-bare the-forests; and-in-His-temple all [say], 'Glory!'

**10** YHWH over-the-flood sat [enthroned]; and-YHWH sits [as] King forever.

**11** YHWH gives strength to-His-people; YHWH blesses His-people with-peace.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **29:1**: Bene elim — 'sons of gods/mighty ones.' The psalm summons the divine council to worship YHWH. This is cosmic, not merely human, worship.

- **29:3-9**: Seven occurrences of 'the voice of the LORD' — the complete, perfect thunderstorm. The number seven signals totality.

— EMET
